name: CN Tower, Toronto
desc: very tall slender concrete tower: three-legged tapering shaft, a round doughnut-shaped main pod two-thirds up (white ring, dark glass band, radome below), a smaller upper pod, long antenna mast with a red aircraft light on top

name: Rogers Centre (SkyDome), Toronto
desc: big round stadium with a white segmented retractable dome roof, low concrete drum with dark glazing around the base

name: Toronto City Hall (new)
desc: two curved concrete towers of different heights facing each other like cupped hands, glass on the inner faces, blank ribbed concrete on the outer faces, a low white saucer-shaped council chamber between them, on a low podium

name: Old City Hall, Toronto
desc: Romanesque Revival sandstone civic building with a tall off-centre clock tower, steep green copper roofs, arched windows

name: Union Station, Toronto
desc: long low Beaux-Arts limestone railway station with a colonnade of Doric columns along the front and a slightly taller central hall

name: First Canadian Place, Toronto
desc: very tall slim square office tower clad in white, strong vertical window stripes, flat roof with a small mechanical box and antenna

name: Toronto-Dominion Centre
desc: a cluster of three austere black steel-and-glass Miesian slab towers of different heights plus a low black banking pavilion

name: Scotia Plaza, Toronto
desc: tall office tower clad in red granite with a stepped, notched top

name: Royal Bank Plaza, Toronto
desc: two triangular towers of different heights with faceted gold-tinted mirrored glass, serrated edges

name: Scotiabank Arena, Toronto
desc: wide low sports arena: stone Art Deco base (old postal building) with a modern stepped grey metal roof on top

name: Roy Thomson Hall, Toronto
desc: round concert hall shaped like an upside-down cupcake: sloping conical curtain of blue-grey diamond-pattern glass, flat round roof

name: Toronto Eaton Centre
desc: long shopping galleria with an arched glass barrel-vault roof running its whole length, plus a mid-rise glass office block attached at one end

name: Ontario Legislative Building (Queen's Park)
desc: wide pink-brown sandstone Romanesque building, big central block with a steep slate hip roof, two small domed copper-topped towers on the wings, rows of arched windows

name: University College, University of Toronto
desc: long Norman-Romanesque stone college building with a square central tower with pointed roof, and a round chapter house with conical roof at one end

name: Royal Ontario Museum, Toronto
desc: heritage buff-brick museum wing with a slate roof, with the Michael Lee-Chin Crystal bursting out of it: jagged interlocking prisms of pale aluminium and glass

name: Casa Loma, Toronto
desc: Gothic Revival castle of grey stone: main hall with red tile roofs, one tall round tower with a red conical roof, one shorter battlemented round tower, chimneys

name: Art Gallery of Ontario
desc: long stone gallery building with a huge curved glass-and-timber facade bulging along the front (Gehry), and a big titanium-blue box rising at the back

name: OCAD University Sharp Centre, Toronto
desc: a white box with black pixel-like square windows floating high in the air on tall, thin, tilted, brightly coloured pencil-like legs (red, yellow, blue, green, purple, orange), above an ordinary brick building

name: St. Lawrence Market, Toronto
desc: long red-brick Victorian market hall with a big pitched roof and a tall arched brick entrance front

name: Gooderham (Flatiron) Building, Toronto
desc: small five-storey red-brick wedge-shaped flatiron building with a rounded prow topped by a green copper cone roof

name: Distillery District, Toronto
desc: group of dark red-brick Victorian industrial buildings with gabled slate roofs, a small white cupola with copper cap, and a tall slim brick chimney

name: Prince Edward Viaduct (Bloor Viaduct), Toronto
desc: long bridge deck on tall stone piers with dark steel arches between the piers

name: Evergreen Brick Works, Toronto
desc: two long low red-brick kiln sheds with pitched roofs and one tall brick chimney

name: R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant, Toronto
desc: Art Deco "palace of purification": long cream-buff brick and limestone buildings with a taller central block and green copper roofs

name: Hearn Generating Station, Toronto
desc: huge long red-brick power station block with tall grid windows and one extremely tall slim concrete smokestack with red and white bands at the top

name: Redpath Sugar refinery, Toronto waterfront
desc: white industrial refinery block with a red rooftop box, three concrete silos beside it, and a dark bulk cargo ship moored alongside

name: Princes' Gates, Exhibition Place, Toronto
desc: white neoclassical triumphal arch topped by a winged victory statue, with curved colonnades of columns sweeping out on both sides

name: BMO Field, Toronto
desc: open-air soccer stadium: green pitch with white markings surrounded by stands on four sides, one stand with red seats

name: CNE midway Ferris wheel
desc: classic fairground Ferris wheel with a red rim, thin spokes, small colourful gondolas, white A-frame supports

name: Ontario Place Cinesphere and pods
desc: white geodesic sphere (triangulated dome) held on thin struts, with three white square pavilion pods raised on stilts beside it

name: Sunnyside Bathing Pavilion, Toronto
desc: long low cream-coloured Beaux-Arts beach pavilion with an arcade of arches, terracotta tile roof and a taller central entrance

name: Humber Bay Arch Bridge, Toronto
desc: white pedestrian bridge with two tall steel arches leaning toward each other and thin hanger cables down to a flat deck

name: Billy Bishop island airport
desc: small low glass terminal building, a short control tower with a dark glass cab, and a small white propeller plane with red tail parked beside it

name: Gibraltar Point Lighthouse, Toronto Islands
desc: old stubby hexagonal stone lighthouse, slightly tapering, with a red lantern room on top

name: Toronto Island ferry
desc: small white double-ended passenger ferry with a row of windows, a red upper deck and one black funnel (on water: draw only the boat)

name: small sailboat
desc: tiny white sailboat with a white mainsail and a pale salmon jib (draw only the boat)

name: four trees
desc: NOT a turnaround: four different trees, one per cell: a round green maple, a dark green pointed spruce, an orange autumn maple, a light green birch. Simple, chunky, same scale

name: Toronto bay-and-gable house
desc: narrow tall Victorian red-brick house with a steep front gable, bay window and a chimney

name: pair of semi-detached houses
desc: two attached narrow brick houses with twin gables, different trim colours, chimneys

name: small two-storey brick house
desc: modest two-storey brick house with a gable roof and a front porch

name: post-war bungalow
desc: small one-storey suburban bungalow with a low gable roof and pale siding

name: island cottage
desc: tiny pastel wooden cottage with a hipped shingle roof and a little porch

name: island cottage, second design
desc: small wooden cottage in a different pastel colour with a hipped roof and a screened porch

name: row of three market shopfronts (Kensington style)
desc: three narrow attached three-storey buildings in different bright colours with striped awnings and shop windows at street level (no readable signs)

name: row of three taller shopfronts
desc: three narrow attached five-storey painted brick buildings in different colours with awnings at street level

name: three-storey brick walk-up
desc: plain three-storey red-brick apartment block with a stone cornice and a wooden water tank on the roof

name: five-storey brick block
desc: five-storey brown-brick commercial block with a stone cornice and regular windows

name: eight-storey brick block
desc: eight-storey red-brick early-1900s office building with a stone cornice and a rooftop water tank

name: collegiate gothic hall
desc: grey stone collegiate-gothic building with a gabled slate roof and a square corner tower with a green copper spire

name: brick warehouse loft
desc: five-storey wide red-brick warehouse loft with large grid windows and a small rooftop box

name: tall brick warehouse loft
desc: seven-storey wide red-brick factory loft with large grid windows and a tall brick chimney at one corner

name: dockside shed
desc: long low corrugated-metal industrial shed with a shallow gable roof

name: dockside shed with containers
desc: long low industrial shed with a shallow gable roof and a few stacked coloured shipping containers beside it

name: grain silos
desc: three tall concrete grain silos side by side with small conical caps and a conveyor gallery across the top

name: exhibition pavilion
desc: four-storey stone exhibition pavilion with a green copper pyramid roof and a flagpole

name: large exhibition pavilion
desc: five-storey buff stone exhibition hall with a green copper pyramid roof and a flagpole

name: mid-rise condo
desc: nine-storey modern condo tower with balconies rising from a wider two-storey stone podium

name: tall condo tower
desc: slim fourteen-storey glass-and-concrete condo tower with balconies on a wider two-storey podium

name: tall condo tower, second design
desc: slim fourteen-storey pale condo tower with balconies on a wider podium, different colour and roof detail

name: glass office tower
desc: fourteen-storey blue glass curtain-wall office tower with a smaller setback top and antenna

name: glass office tower with pyramid top
desc: fourteen-storey teal glass office tower with a low pyramid roof

name: bank office block
desc: nine-storey broad dark-blue glass bank tower with a mechanical box on the roof

name: bank tower
desc: fifteen-storey broad blue glass bank tower with a setback crown and antenna

name: bank tower with pyramid top
desc: fifteen-storey broad blue-green glass bank tower with a low pyramid roof
